title: Predictive admission-control and cost-aware autoscaler for embeddings
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement:
The current embeddings router scales reactively which leads to two operational issues: 1) repeated late autoscale scoops under bursty traffic causing high p99 tail latency, and 2) unnecessary GPU spin-up/tear-down cycles that increase cost for sustained moderate growth. Additionally, current admission control is coarse (reject or accept) and does not consider per-tenant burst credits or cost impact.

Goal:
Design and implement a predictive autoscaler + admission-control layer for the embeddings endpoint that: (a) forecasts short-term request arrivals to pre-warm capacity and avoid p99 latency spikes, (b) applies cost-aware scaling decisions (weighing expected token cost vs. additional GPU hours), and (c) offers graceful degradation via priority-based admission and burst credit accounting per tenant.

Non-goals:
This ticket does NOT change core model kernels or quantization profiles, nor does it modify embedding model accuracy. It focuses on orchestration, admission, and scaling logic and the associated telemetry.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- SLO: reduce p99 embedding request latency under 8k token workload by >= 30% during burst events captured in our synthetic traffic tests.
- Cost: reduce unnecessary scale-ups (spin-ups within 5 minutes of previous scale-down) by >= 20% for production traffic baselines.
- Fairness: ensure no tenant loses more than 5% of successful requests due to admission control compared to baseline when within paid burst allowances.
- Observability: expose metrics for forecast error (MAPE), admission-rate by priority, burst-credit balances, and decision rationale logs for each scale event.

Design summary:
1) Short-term forecasting: implement an arrival-rate forecaster using a lightweight ensemble (Holt-Winters + exponential smoothing + recent-window linear trend) running every 10s per route/tenant-class to predict next 1-5 minute arrival rate. Keep model state in memory with checkpointed snapshots to Redis for fast recovery.
2) Cost-aware autoscaler: extend the existing autoscaling policy to consume forecasted load and compute an expected cost delta for candidate scale actions (gpus to add/remove). Cost model inputs: expected tokens/sec, per-GPU throughput (tokens/sec) by model/quantization, estimated spin-up time, and reserved burst credits. The autoscaler will prefer horizontal scaling within same instance type before bursting to higher-cost hot pools.
3) Admission & burst credits: implement a token-bucket style burst credit ledger per tenant (credit accrual tied to committed usage) with priority classes: realtime, standard, background. When forecasted load exceeds safe capacity, admission decisions will first shed background, then standard, preserving realtime requests until critical thresholds. Admission responses will return structured headers explaining reason and remaining burst credits.
4) Soft pre-warm + staged spin-up: use forecast confidence to decide pre-warm (booting instances with reduced priority) vs. immediate full spin-up. Pre-warmed instances accept lower-priority traffic and can be promoted if pressure persists.
5) Fallback routing: if scale-up exceeds configured latency budget, route requests to compatible lower-cost model variants (smaller embedder) as graceful degradation; annotate responses with variant used.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Forecast metrics: predicted vs observed rate, MAPE(1m/5m), lead time used for decisioning.
- Scaling events: reason, forecast snapshot, expected cost delta, actual scale result, spin-up time observed.
- Admission logs: tenant, priority, decision, remaining burst credits.
- Budget burn-rate: estimated $/hour change per autoscale decision.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for forecast correctness (synthetic seasonality & bursts).
- Staging chaos tests: replay traffic traces from last 6 months (including Black Friday-style bursts) and compare p95/p99 and scale events vs baseline.
- Controlled canary in prod: route 5% of traffic from low-variance tenants through the new path for 48h with auto-rollback if forecast error > 40% or p99 degrades.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement forecasting service + metrics, disabled by default.
2) Enable cost-aware autoscaler in staging with simulated cost weights.
3) Canary with background-priority tenants for 48h.
4) Expand to multi-tenant with per-tenant burst credits.
5) Full production toggle after two successful 7-day canaries.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Forecast complexity vs. operational overhead: we picked a simple ensemble to minimize risk, but heavier LSTM/RNN models would yield better forecasts for some tenants. Decision: defer ML models to follow-up once infra is stable.
- Where to persist burst ledger: Redis vs. strongly consistent store (Spanner-like). Decision: use Redis with write-through persistence for speed and design an idempotent reconciliation job.
- Cost model friction: per-GPU throughput varies by model/seq-len. We'll start with 3 canonical profiles and add auto-calibration later.

Integration links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Predictive+Autoscale
- Prototype forecaster repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/emb-forecast-proto/pull/4
- Related infra PR for pre-warm lifecycle: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/792

Deployment and ops runbook snippets:
- If forecast MAPE > 50% for 15m: disable pre-warm and revert to reactive autoscaler; page on-call.
- If admission rate > 10% for >10m: throttle standard priority and notify PM/CS teams with tenant list.

Notes on backwards compatibility:
- All clients continue to use same REST API. Admission decisions return 429 with structured JSON explaining burst credits and retry-after where applicable. New headers added are backwards-compatible optional fields.
